---
title: "Multi-Service Users"
description: "Share of users who have signed in to two or more public services."
---

The share of CanadaLogin users who have used it to sign in to two or more public
services, out of users who have signed in to at least one.

One account for many government services is one of CanadaLogin's main benefits.
This metric measures how often that happens. It counts services, not
applications, and leaves out internal CanadaLogin components.

## Calculation

Read successful events from
[`application_usage`](../../catalog/ibm_verify_events_raw/application_usage.qmd)
with a known user ID (not blank or `"UNKNOWN"`). Map each `applicationid` to its
service through [`rp.alias`](../../catalog/rp/alias.qmd) and
[`rp.service`](../../catalog/rp/service.qmd), and keep only services that are not
internal. Drop events before the service's `launch_date`, which are pre-launch
testing. Count the distinct services each user has reached up to the end date,
then divide users with two or more by users with at least one.

The end date is an ET day (America/Toronto). Leave out the end date to measure
up to the latest event.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
WITH public_aliases AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        al.alias AS applicationid,
        s.service_name_en,
        CAST(s.launch_date AS DATE) AS launch_date
    FROM rp.alias al
    JOIN rp.service s ON al.rp_id = s.rp_id
    WHERE NOT s.is_internal
),
events AS (
    SELECT
        userid,
        applicationid,
        -- time is a UTC string; report on ET days
        date(with_timezone(CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp), 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto') AS et_day
    FROM ibm_verify_events_raw.application_usage
    WHERE result = 'success'
      AND userid IS NOT NULL
      AND userid NOT IN ('', 'UNKNOWN')
),
user_services AS (
    SELECT
        e.userid,
        count(DISTINCT p.service_name_en) AS services
    FROM events e
    JOIN public_aliases p ON e.applicationid = p.applicationid
    -- events before launch are pre-launch testing
    WHERE e.et_day >= p.launch_date
      AND e.et_day <= DATE '2026-11-15'
    GROUP BY e.userid
)

SELECT
    count(*) AS users,
    count_if(services >= 2) AS multi_service_users,
    CAST(count_if(services >= 2) AS DOUBLE) / count(*) AS multi_service_share
FROM user_services;
```

## R

```r
public_aliases <- tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "alias")) |>
  inner_join(tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "service")), by = "rp_id") |>
  filter(!is_internal) |>
  distinct(applicationid = alias, service_name_en, launch_date)

tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_raw", "application_usage")) |>
  filter(
    result == "success",
    !is.na(userid), !userid %in% c("", "UNKNOWN")
  ) |>
  # time is a UTC string; report on ET days
  mutate(et_day = sql("date(with_timezone(CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp), 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto')")) |>
  inner_join(public_aliases, by = "applicationid") |>
  # events before launch are pre-launch testing
  filter(
    et_day >= as.Date(launch_date),
    et_day <= as.Date("2026-11-15")
  ) |>
  group_by(userid) |>
  summarise(services = n_distinct(service_name_en), .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(
    users = n(),
    multi_service_users = sum(as.integer(services >= 2), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(multi_service_share = as.numeric(multi_service_users) / users)
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

**Online services, not applications.** Related applications of one service
count as one service, through the registry in
[`rp.alias`](../../catalog/rp/alias.qmd). For example, MyCGC runs two
applications in IBM Verify (.NET and Power Pages), and a user who reaches both
counts as one service. Counting by application instead would miscount
those users as multi-service.

**The denominator is users who have used at least one service, not all
CanadaLogin accounts.** It counts users who have signed in to at least one
public service. Accounts that never reached one, such as those that stopped at
sign-up or only used internal CanadaLogin components, are left out. See [New
Accounts and Idle Account Rate](new-accounts-and-idle-rate.qmd) for those.

**Since launch, not a window.** The share covers every event up to the end date,
so it tends to grow as users have more time to reach a second service. To count
services reached within a window instead, add a start date next to the end date.

## Alternative names

- multi-service share
- users of two or more services
- cross-service users
- service breadth
- one account, many services
